bibl.title: Multiculturalism, Culture Mixing, and Prejudice: Effects of Priming Chinese Diversity Models Among Hong Kong University Students

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: Study 2 compared multiculturalism, assimilation, or control primes’ effects, and found that the multiculturalism prime, through increased positive emotions, indirectly reduced social distancing from Mainland Chinese and disgust toward culture mixing, and increased Chinese ethnic identity and multicultural identity styles; the assimilation prime had the opposite indirect effects through increasing negative emotions.

span.label: priming of cultural diversity models
span.quote: In these studies, we examined the effects on Hong Kong residents of presenting cultural diversity within China in terms of either multiculturalism or assimilation.

span.label: behavioural-experiment
span.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: assimilation prime (N = 54), multiculturalism prime (N = 58), or control (N = 56).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Reading a societal diversity model first elicits an emotional reaction, and that emotional reaction is what carries the prime through to intergroup attitudes and identity
span.quote: Thus, we propose that priming societal models that relate to outgroups could elicit emotional responses; specifically, especially among a young university student population, multicultural primes might lead to more positive emotions than assimilation primes, which could serve as the underlying processes that explain their effects on attitudes toward outgroups.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: A multicultural frame lowers the perceived threat to the local culture, which raises the perceived compatibility of the two cultures and so reduces disgust at their mixing
span.quote: It is likely that to the degree that multiculturalism reduced Hongkongers’ perceived sense of threat, it enhanced the perceived compatibility of these cultures, as shown by reduced disgust toward mixed cultural symbols and increased integration of Chinese and Hong Kong identities; while assimilation had the opposite effects.

span.label: Both studies were underpowered for the effect sizes assumed.
span.quote: The two studies were slightly underpowered due to limited sample size.

span.label: Convenience sample of Hong Kong university students limits generalisation.
span.quote: In addition, the two studies also employed convenience sampling methods among Hong Kong university students, which may not generalize to all sectors of the Hong Kong population.

span.label: Identity measures were placed after the manipulation, so they could not be used as moderators.
span.quote: In these studies, we conceptualized identity measures as dependent variables and included them immediately after the experimental manipulations, precluding their use as individualdifference moderators of reactions.

span.label: Because the two identity styles were outcomes rather than predictors, their distinct functions could not be separated.
span.quote: Moreover, as the two multicultural identity styles were examined as outcomes rather than predictors, the distinctions between hybrid identity style and alternating identity style that can be found through controlling for one another (Ward et al., 2018) and thus more complex features of these cultural identities could not be thoroughly examined.

span.label: multiculturalism
span.quote: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: assimilation
span.quote: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: colorblindness
span.quote: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: social distance
span.quote: Desire to keep one’s social distance from outgroups (Bogardus, 1925, 1947), ranging from being unwilling to marry an outgroup member up to even being unwilling to live in the same city

span.label: culture mixing
span.quote: In our globalized world, culture mixing is an everyday phenomenon, commonly depicted in logos and international brands that show different cultural symbols coexisting together, or even combining and fusing together

span.label: social distancing
span.quote: Study 2 compared multiculturalism, assimilation, or control primes’ effects, and found that the multiculturalism prime, through increased positive emotions, indirectly reduced social distancing from Mainland Chinese and disgust toward culture mixing, and increased Chinese ethnic identity and multicultural identity styles; the assimilation prime had the opposite indirect effects through increasing negative emotions

span.label: multiculturalism against assimilation and colorblindness - THREE DIVERSITY MODELS ON ONE AXIS, and the axis is stated: whether cultural difference is APPRECIATED or IGNORED. Colorblindness and assimilation are put on the same side, which is a grouping this literature does not always make
span.quote: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: social distance, as measured here - a construct defined by the EXTENT of contact refused, from marriage down to co-residence in a city. The scale is the definition, which is what makes `prejudice` operational in this design
span.quote: Desire to keep one’s social distance from outgroups (Bogardus, 1925, 1947), ranging from being unwilling to marry an outgroup member up to even being unwilling to live in the same city

span.label: the prime, in this study - not a word list or a photograph but A DESCRIPTION OF THE READER'S OWN COUNTRY: a passage about how China handles diversity, read by Hong Kong students who are both minority and majority culture members. The manipulation is a national self-description
span.quote: Results show new evidence of the importance of emotion in how non-immigrant regional groups, who are both minority and majority culture members, react to different diversity models

span.label: contradicts → Verkuyten (2005), on multiculturalism priming among Turkish minorities in the Netherlands
span.quote: This is dissimilar from previous research among Turkish minorities in the Netherlands, where priming multiculturalism tended to decrease outgroup evaluations relative to ingroup evaluations (Verkuyten, 2005).

span.label: builds-on → Todd and Galinsky (2012) multiculturalism priming materials
span.quote: The instructions and Multiculturalism priming material were adapted from previous research in the United States (Todd and Galinsky, 2012) with content modified through group discussions to fit the Hong Kong cultural context.

span.label: builds-on → Stone and Crisp (2007) superordinate-identity assimilation priming material
span.quote: The priming material was adapted from a previous study about assimilating into superordinate identities (Stone and Crisp, 2007) and modified to emphasize the assimilation process.

span.label: extends → Morrison et al. (2010), on symbolic threat as mediator of reactions to multiculturalism primes
span.quote: The results are an interesting complement to findings of Morrison et al. (2010), who found that White Americans’ negative reaction to multiculturalism primes (vs. color-blindness) was mediated by their sense of symbolic threat; here, we find that Hong Kong participants’ negative reaction to an assimilation prime (vs. multiculturalism) was mediated by more negative emotional reactions.

span.label: multiculturalism —distinct-from→ assimilation
span.note: differs in: WHETHER CULTURAL DIFFERENCE IS APPRECIATED OR IGNORED - the paper states the axis rather than leaving it to be inferred, and puts colorblindness on the ignoring side with assimilation · strength of the relation: 0.95 — Two edges come out of this one clause. The grouping is the part worth noting: colorblindness and assimilation are often distinguished elsewhere and are treated here as one side of a single contrast.
span.quote: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: multiculturalism —distinct-from→ colorblindness
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — The second half of the same contrast, kept as its own edge because a reader searching for either model should meet the axis at the same place.
span.quote: Models of Cultural Diversity Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: multiculturalism —causes→ social distancing
span.note: direction on the measure: reduces · strength of the relation: 0.85 — INDIRECT, and the paper says so: the route is through increased positive emotions, not directly. The same sentence reports the assimilation prime producing the opposite effects through negative emotions, which is the symmetry the design was built for.
span.quote: Study 2 compared multiculturalism, assimilation, or control primes’ effects, and found that the multiculturalism prime, through increased positive emotions, indirectly reduced social distancing from Mainland Chinese and disgust toward culture mixing, and increased Chinese ethnic identity and multicultural identity styles; the assimilation prime had the opposite indirect effects through increasing negative emotions

span.label: assimilation —causes→ social distancing
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.8 — The mirror edge, and weighted slightly lower because `the opposite indirect effects` is stated by reference to the first result rather than reported in its own terms here.
span.quote: Study 2 compared multiculturalism, assimilation, or control primes’ effects, and found that the multiculturalism prime, through increased positive emotions, indirectly reduced social distancing from Mainland Chinese and disgust toward culture mixing, and increased Chinese ethnic identity and multicultural identity styles; the assimilation prime had the opposite indirect effects through increasing negative emotions

span.label: t-test
span.quote: Analyses testing the priming effects between two conditions were conducted in JASP (JASP Team, 2018) using independent sample t-tests

span.label: ANOVA
span.quote: An overall ANOVA predicting positive emotion from the three priming conditions showed that the primes had statistically significant different impact, F(2,165) = 15.19, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.16.

span.label: eta squared (effect size)
span.quote: An overall ANOVA predicting positive emotion from the three priming conditions showed that the primes had statistically significant different impact, F(2,165) = 15.19, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.16.

span.label: chi-squared test
span.quote: The Chi-square test also showed no gender difference between conditions

span.label: ANCOVA
span.quote: Subsequent ANCOVA tests with conditions as fixed factor, age and gender as covariates demonstrated the same priming effects as discussed above.

span.label: Tukey post hoc correction
span.quote: Post hoc analyses with Tukey correction showed that participants in the multiculturalism (MC) prime group (M = 1.14, SD = 1.38) had higher positive emotion compared to the assimilation (A) prime group (M = −0.16, SD = 1.42), t = 5.45, p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.93

span.label: effect size (Cohen's d) with confidence interval
span.term: effect size (Cohen's d) with confidence interval
span.quote: The results showed that the multiculturalism (MC) priming significantly reduced social distancing compared to the control condition, t(116) = −2.19, p = 0.03, Cohen’s d = 0.40, 95% CI = [0.04,0.77]

span.label: Pearson correlation
span.quote: TABLE 1 | Study 1: Bivariate Pearson Correlations.

span.label: Cronbach's alpha (internal consistency)
span.quote: The scale yielded excellent reliability, McDonald’s ω = 0.90 and Cronbach’s α = 0.90.

span.label: McDonald's omega (internal consistency)
span.quote: The scale yielded excellent reliability, McDonald’s ω = 0.90 and Cronbach’s α = 0.90.

span.label: mediation / path analysis with maximum likelihood and robust standard errors
span.term: mediation / path analysis with maximum likelihood and robust standard errors
span.quote: The proposed mediation models were tested in path analysis using lavaan (Rosseel, 2012) and joint significance of indirect paths were estimated by maximum likelihood estimation with robust standard errors.

span.label: Monte Carlo simulation power analysis
span.quote: A post hoc power analysis using package “mc_power_med” (Schoemann et al., 2017) with Monte Carlo simulation method showed a moderate to high level of power for detecting these indirect effects.

span.label: Mahalanobis distance (outlier exclusion)
span.quote: Additionally, data from three participants were excluded based on Mahalanobis distance

span.label: In Study 1 the multiculturalism prime lowered desire for social distance from Mainland Chinese relative to no prime, but left disgust toward culture mixing and national identity strength unchanged.
span.quote: In summary, compared to a noprime control, the multiculturalism prime significantly decreased social distancing but had no statistically significant effects on disgust toward Hong Kong-Mainland culture mixing or national identity strength.

span.label: In Study 2 the three primes produced direct effects only on emotion and on ethnic Chinese identity strength; social distancing, disgust and both identity styles showed no direct priming effect.
span.quote: Summarizing the above, we found a significant effect of priming conditions only on emotions and ethnic identity strength, but not on HIS, AIS, social distancing, or disgust toward culture mixing.

span.label: Relative to control, the multiculturalism prime raised positive emotion and thereby indirectly cut disgust toward culture mixing and raised ethnic identity strength, hybrid identity style and alternating identity style, with a marginal indirect reduction in social distancing.
span.quote: Compared to control, the multiculturalism prime, through increasing positive emotion, marginally reduced social distancing and significantly reduced disgust; it also significantly increased ethnic identity strength, HIS, and AIS.

span.label: The assimilation prime produced the mirror-image indirect pattern, lowering positive emotion and thereby increasing social distancing and disgust while decreasing ethnic identity strength and both multicultural identity styles.
span.quote: On the contrary, through reducing positive emotion, the assimilation prime, significantly increased social distancing and disgust; it also significantly decreased ethnic identity strength, HIS, and AIS.

span.label: Reading that Hong Kong is being assimilated into China directly weakened participants' ethnic Chinese identity compared with the control condition, a defensive response.
span.quote: Post hoc tests with Tukey correction showed that ethnic identity strength decreased under the assimilation prime (M = 3.38, SD = 1.76) compared to both the control (M = 3.93, SD = 1.25)

span.label: Breaking the affect composite apart, the beneficial multiculturalism effects ran specifically through pride, happiness and interest.
span.quote: Here, the exploratory analyses suggested that the positive effects of multiculturalism priming went through increasing pride, happiness and feeling interested

span.label: multiculturalism (as a diversity model)
span.quote: Multiculturalism emphasizes the appreciation of different cultural values, traditions, and lifestyles, in contrast to colorblindness or assimilation, which reflect a preference toward ignoring cultural differences

span.label: hybrid identity style (HIS) vs alternating identity style (AIS)
span.term: hybrid identity style (HIS) vs alternating identity style (AIS)
span.quote: Those who perceive these two identities are simultaneously compatible may endorse a hybrid identity style (HIS), while those who think the two identities are both valid but should be adopted in different contexts may endorse an alternating identity style (AIS)

span.label: Positive Emotion (the study's composite affect index)
span.term: Positive Emotion (the study's composite affect index)
span.quote: To simplify results description, a combination of positive minus negative affect, termed “Positive Emotion,” was calculated by subtracting the mean score of negative affect from positive affect.

span.label: social distance
span.quote: Desire to keep one’s social distance from outgroups (Bogardus, 1925, 1947), ranging from being unwilling to marry an outgroup member up to even being unwilling to live in the same city, is a significant indicator of prejudice in intergroup relations

span.label: priming condition (multiculturalism / assimilation / control)
span.quote: Participants were randomly assigned to one of three groups: assimilation prime (N = 54), multiculturalism prime (N = 58), or control (N = 56).

span.label: social distancing from Mainland Chinese
span.quote: Social distancing from Mainland Chinese was measured using the Bogardus Social Distance Scale adopted from Miller and Salkind (2002).

span.label: disgust toward Hong Kong-Mainland culture mixing
span.term: disgust toward Hong Kong-Mainland culture mixing
span.quote: Disgust toward culture mixing was measured by same images and disgust ratings as used in Study 1.

span.label: multicultural identity styles (hybrid and alternating)
span.quote: Multicultural identity styles (i.e., Hybrid Identity Style [HIS] and Alternating Identity Style [AIS]) were measured using the scale developed by Ward et al. (2018).

span.label: positive and negative affective response to the prime
span.term: positive and negative affective response to the prime
span.quote: Hypothesis 4. Positive and negative affective responses will mediate the priming effects on social distancing, disgust toward culture mixing, ethnic identity strength, and multicultural identity styles.

span.label: age and gender
span.quote: Subsequent ANCOVA tests with conditions as fixed factor, age and gender as covariates demonstrated the same priming effects as discussed above.

span.label: n = 118 — final analysed sample of Study 1, split 57 primed and 61 no-prime
span.quote: The final sample for data analysis consisted of 118 participants (87 females, 30 males and 1 unreported, Mage = 21.69, SD = 4.69) with 57 participants in the priming condition and 61 participants in the no prime condition.

span.label: 168 — sample size of Study 2, which the authors call slightly underpowered
span.quote: Given the sample size of 168 participants, this study is therefore slightly underpowered.

span.label: t(116) = −2.19, p = 0.03, d = 0.40 — Study 1 effect of the multiculturalism prime on social distancing
span.quote: The results showed that the multiculturalism (MC) priming significantly reduced social distancing compared to the control condition, t(116) = −2.19, p = 0.03, Cohen’s d = 0.40, 95% CI = [0.04,0.77]

span.label: F(2,165) = 15.19, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.16 — overall Study 2 effect of priming condition on positive emotion
span.quote: An overall ANOVA predicting positive emotion from the three priming conditions showed that the primes had statistically significant different impact, F(2,165) = 15.19, p < 0.001, η2 = 0.16.

span.label: Cohen’s d = 0.93 — size of the positive-emotion gap between the multiculturalism and assimilation prime groups
span.quote: Post hoc analyses with Tukey correction showed that participants in the multiculturalism (MC) prime group (M = 1.14, SD = 1.38) had higher positive emotion compared to the assimilation (A) prime group (M = −0.16, SD = 1.42), t = 5.45, p < 0.001, Cohen’s d = 0.93

span.label: ω = 0.90 and α = 0.90 — internal reliability of the Study 1 social distancing scale
span.quote: The scale yielded excellent reliability, McDonald’s ω = 0.90 and Cronbach’s α = 0.90.
